title: Comparative Politics
topics: Nature and scope of comparative politics

items.q: Which term is described by “an outlook in which people scarcely identify with the wider country and expect little from central authority”?
o: Post-materialism
Subject culture
Parochial culture
Political socialisation
items.s: Parochial culture is an outlook in which people scarcely identify with the wider country and expect little from central authority.

items.q: The statement “the practice of dividing the assembly into two chambers that deliberate separately over legislation” describes which of the following?
o: Bicameralism
Head of state
Vote of no confidence
Cabinet
items.s: Bicameralism is the practice of dividing the assembly into two chambers that deliberate separately over legislation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the defined area whose electors choose one or more of the members of the assembly”?
o: Single transferable vote
First past the post
Constituency
Proportional representation
items.s: Constituency is the defined area whose electors choose one or more of the members of the assembly.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Most similar systems design.
o: an organised group that seeks to win public office by contesting elections under a common label
the direct effort to persuade legislators or officials by supplying information, arguments or inducements
a characteristic that can take more than one value across places or periods and is used to explain or be explained
a way of comparing places alike in many respects so that the few remaining differences account for the outcome
items.s: Most similar systems design: a way of comparing places alike in many respects so that the few remaining differences account for the outcome. The other options describe Lobbying, Variable, Political party.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Political party?
o: the weakening of rules and offices as they are captured by particular concerns and used for private gain
an organised group that seeks to win public office by contesting elections under a common label
the sphere of voluntary associations, religious bodies and independent media standing between the household and the state
the ceremonial or symbolic first figure of a country, who may hold little everyday authority
items.s: Political party: an organised group that seeks to win public office by contesting elections under a common label. The other options describe Head of state, Political decay, Civil society.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Social movement?
o: a loose sustained campaign by many people outside established channels, pressing for change in values or policy
an outlook in which people see themselves as entitled and able to influence decisions
an organisation of a few prominent figures with loose membership and little continuous mass activity
the doctrine that those who govern must act within stated limits and can be held to them
items.s: Social movement: a loose sustained campaign by many people outside established channels, pressing for change in values or policy. The other options describe Cadre party, Participant culture, Constitutionalism.

items.q: Parliamentary system may be defined as
o: the process through which people acquire their orientations towards authority, first in the family and later at school and work
a way of comparing places alike in many respects so that the few remaining differences account for the outcome
an arrangement in which the administration is drawn from and can be removed by the elected assembly
an outlook in which people are aware of central authority and affected by it but take no active part
items.s: Parliamentary system: an arrangement in which the administration is drawn from and can be removed by the elected assembly. The other options describe Political socialisation, Most similar systems design, Subject culture.

items.q: Monopoly of violence may be defined as
o: an outlook in which people see themselves as entitled and able to influence decisions
the claim of the organised apparatus to be the only body entitled to use force within its borders
a way of comparing places alike in many respects so that the few remaining differences account for the outcome
the sphere of voluntary associations, religious bodies and independent media standing between the household and the state
items.s: Monopoly of violence: the claim of the organised apparatus to be the only body entitled to use force within its borders. The other options describe Civil society, Participant culture, Most similar systems design.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Comparative politics?
o: a loose sustained campaign by many people outside established channels, pressing for change in values or policy
the systematic study of how different countries organise their public decision making and with what consequences
a voter's lasting sense of belonging to one organisation and habit of supporting it
the passage from restricted rule to open contestation, usually involving a pact among contending elites
items.s: Comparative politics: the systematic study of how different countries organise their public decision making and with what consequences. The other options describe Party identification, Democratic transition, Social movement.
items.t: Nature and scope of comparative politics

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Cadre party?
o: the body of fundamental rules that establishes the main offices of a country and limits their powers
an organisation of a few prominent figures with loose membership and little continuous mass activity
a formal expression by the assembly that it no longer supports the administration, usually obliging it to resign
the body of people and arrangements that holds authority to make rules for a country at a given time
items.s: Cadre party: an organisation of a few prominent figures with loose membership and little continuous mass activity. The other options describe Government, Vote of no confidence, Constitution.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Political decay?
o: the fundamental pattern of rules and offices through which authority is exercised, apart from whoever currently holds it
a loose sustained campaign by many people outside established channels, pressing for change in values or policy
the weakening of rules and offices as they are captured by particular concerns and used for private gain
a country whose people are largely united by a shared identity and whose borders are recognised abroad
items.s: Political decay: the weakening of rules and offices as they are captured by particular concerns and used for private gain. The other options describe Social movement, Regime, Nation state.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Comparative politics.
o: a rule in which electors rank candidates and surplus marks pass to the next preferences until seats are filled
rule in which office holders treat public resources and posts as personal property to be used and passed on
the systematic study of how different countries organise their public decision making and with what consequences
the practice of examining several places side by side in order to test explanations and draw general conclusions
items.s: Comparative politics: the systematic study of how different countries organise their public decision making and with what consequences. The other options describe Comparative method, Patrimonialism, Single transferable vote.

the process through which people acquire their orientations towards authority, first in the family and later at school and work
the body of people and arrangements that holds authority to make rules for a country at a given time

items.q: Case study may be defined as

Political decay
Oligarchy
Authoritarianism

the defined area whose electors choose one or more of the members of the assembly
the distortion that arises when the places examined are chosen in a way that favours a preferred conclusion
a division of authority in which central and regional governments each hold powers the other cannot withdraw
items.s: Selection bias: the distortion that arises when the places examined are chosen in a way that favours a preferred conclusion. The other options describe Constituency, Democracy, Federalism.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Political socialisation.

the passage from restricted rule to open contestation, usually involving a pact among contending elites
the process through which people acquire their orientations towards authority, first in the family and later at school and work
